{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows negative sentiment (e.g., -0.25 or 0.00 with recent negative spikes) as models tend to overreact.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility in early periods (e.g., first 5-7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — models often overshoot downward.",
    "Increase forecast bias toward historical mean when sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is trending away from recent 15-day average — indicates mean reversion.",
    "Apply upward correction if model forecast is significantly below true outcome after a recent spike — suggests rebound or sentiment shift.",
    "Avoid over-optimistic forecasts when sentiment history includes multiple 0.00 entries — models may be overfitting to recent noise.",
    "If sentiment history shows increasing positivity (e.g., 0.00 → 0.33 → 0.50), gradually increase forecast bias upward to reflect sentiment momentum.",
    "Correct for lagged price movements — if true outcome is rising while model is still reacting to prior lows, adjust forecast upward by 5-10% of recent 15-day range."
  ]
}
